review_type: source-grounded AI review; not physician adjudication
reviewed_components: all clinical facts and measured quantities
corrections: Creatinine 8.6 mg/dL (text, on the day of admission; p1-f053) and 10.5 (Table 1 Day 1, days following paraquat ingestion; p1-f104) restored from ambiguous/review_only to supported/include: the source does not equate Day 1 with the admission day, so they are two literal time points, not one measurement in conflict; the ambiguity and article limitation were rewritten accordingly.

Unmerged the Overall-vital-signs sentence from the pulse sentence (p1-f042) and the On-arrival blood pressure (p1-f043): matching numbers alone do not make them the same measurement, and the normal flag no longer transfers to the timed On-arrival value. Added p1-f190 (pulse 71 beats/min, flag normal) and p1-f191 (blood pressure 90/60 mm Hg, flag normal) from the Overall sentence, consistent with the already separate p1-f044/p1-f045; linked them to event p1-e08 and the vital-signs ambiguity.

Added four supported relations: treatments during admission (p1-e16), hemodialysis started early after the admission (p1-e21) and the day-of-admission urea/creatinine (p1-e14) each before the discharge (p1-e24) (in-hospital care before the discharge ending the stay); oral lesions on examination (p1-e08) before the nystatin prescribed for the oral lesions (p1-e17) (finding before the action about it).
unresolved: Figure captions in source.json are only the labels Figure 1 to Figure 3. The original JATS (raw.xml) holds a short <statement> for each figure that was not captured as a segment, so it cannot be quoted as evidence: Figure 1 "Oral ulcerations and edematous lip."; Figure 2 "X-ray chest posteroanterior (PA) view showing mild bilateral patchy consolidation especially in hilum." (the case text says the initial chest x-ray was normal); Figure 3 "CT-scan of the thorax without contrast day 2 following paraquat poisoning showed sub- segmental collapses in the right costophrenic area." None of these is recorded as a fact.

Table 1 prints no units, uses decimal commas in many cells (kept as printed text with no numeric value) and does not expand the NA and K headers; every cell is recorded with its Day label and the caption anchor "paraquat ingestion".

The Table 1 caption anchors Day 1 to Day 9 to paraquat ingestion, while the text places referral 7 days after ingestion and gives admission and discharge values that match Day 1 BUN and Day 9 values; this is not reconciled (see ambiguities).

Creatinine on the day of admission is 8.6 in the text versus 10.5 in Table 1 Day 1; the source does not equate Day 1 with the day of admission, so both are kept as separate time points (see ambiguities). The Table 1 Day 5 BUN printed as 3,4 is quarantined as a probable print artefact.
Source conflict: the case text says an unknown quantity of a liquid was ingested while the Discussion says a low dose of paraquat was ingested; both quantity facts are review_only.
Several case-text sentences are garbled (for example "auscultationl.The", "three cessation of dialysis", the verbless Ventolin and becotide treatments); recorded literally without repair.
Visual status of figures is not_inspected in this file; the three images were inspected in visual.json.

key_findings: All 90 Table 1 cells checked programmatically and by eye against segments b00006-b00014: value text, Day label, caption anchor, no added units, decimal-comma cells kept as text without numeric value.

Table 1 Day labels stay anchored literally to paraquat ingestion; text admission and discharge values (urea 212, BUN 19, Cr 1.3, Cr 8.6) are not merged with Day 1 or Day 9 cells because the source never says they are the same measurement.
Day 5 BUN printed 3,4 kept as printed and quarantined as an ambiguous probable print artefact (ambiguity, not conflict).
Unknown quantity (case text) versus low dose (Discussion) kept as a source conflict on the quantity attribute only, both sides review_only.

Verbless Ventolin nebulizer and becotide spray accepted as administered (listed as other treatments following admission alongside received antibiotics) with an ambiguity; multi-target comprehensive therapy kept as a medication regimen with an ambiguity that it is not equated with the Qilu scheme.

Both dialysis facts and both referral facts left unmerged with ambiguities; every original relation's full evidence list re-read and each states the order (ingestion anchors, Day column labels, because/after wording).

Figures viewed at full resolution: F1 lower-face oral photograph, F2 frontal chest radiograph, F3 photographed four-slice chest CT montage with burned-in patient text; visual, figure-EHR, privacy and measurement-series sidecars consistent with pixels and Table 1.
residual_risks: Figure captions live in JATS <statement> elements not captured in source.json; they are only noted as a limitation and the Figure 2 statement (patchy consolidation) differs from the text's normal initial chest x-ray.
Table 1 timing (days following ingestion) is internally inconsistent with referral 7 days after ingestion; a reader may still assume Day 1 is the admission day.
Ventolin/becotide administration rests on a garbled verbless sentence.
